claim: The deployment runs 4x CMP 170HX with VRAM unlocked to 64 GB per card, giving 256 GB of aggregate HBM2e on the box.
stance_target: The repo's claim that the box has 320 GB of HBM2e after unlock (5 cards x 64 GB)
quoted_support: By leveraging the GA100 silicon (sm_80) and unlocking the VRAM to 64 GB per card, the system achieves the model's full 1,047,736-token context ceiling

claim: PP4 with DSpark reaches 98.1 tok/s single-stream decode versus 50.8 tok/s for plain PP4, and 90.0 versus 38.8 tok/s at 100k context.
stance_target: The repo's reported 98 tok/s decode figure on 4x CMP 170HX
quoted_support: Decode (Single Stream) 50.8 tok/s -> 98.1 tok/s ... Decode @ 100k Context 38.8 tok/s -> 90.0 tok/s

claim: Prefill at 77k context measures 5,272 tok/s on plain PP4 and 5,207 tok/s with DSpark.
stance_target: The repo's reported ~5,300 tok/s prefill figure

claim: PWRBRK# on pin B30 can force the cards into a low-power state on certain motherboards, reducing performance by about 4x.
stance_target: The repo's PWRBRK# power-brake trap and its ~4x performance penalty claim
scope_conditions: CMP 170HX on motherboards that assert PWRBRK# on edge pin B30
quoted_support: A critical deployment factor is the PWRBRK# (pin B30) diagnostic; on certain motherboards, this signal can force the cards into a low-power state, reducing performance by ~4x.

claim: The cards are limited to PCIe Gen2 x4 in this deployment.
stance_target: The repo's PCIe Gen2 x4 fabric claim
quoted_support: While it lacks display outputs and is limited to PCIe Gen2 x4, it offers 64 GB of HBM2e memory once the VRAM is unlocked.

claim: The 6.6x PP-over-TP prefill advantage is attributed specifically to the PCIe Gen2 x4 bandwidth constraint of the CMP 170HX.
stance_target: The repo's causal claim that the fabric, not the software stack, is what rules out TP
quoted_support: On this specific hardware, Pipeline Parallelism provides a 6.6x prefill advantage over Tensor Parallelism due to the severe PCIe Gen2 x4 bandwidth constraints of the CMP 170HX.
